result_semantic_payload.summary: The scope contains exactly three live files and a single filesystem timeline cluster; there are no Windows account, logon, execution, registry or event-log artifacts at all, so no device-user attribution can be established from system telemetry. The only user-attributable activity is the content of /chat/wangfang.log, three first-person chat messages by "wangfang" at 2024-04-10 21:02, 21:05 and 21:31 (financial stress / selling a car; a dinner with "老张" at month-end; "got home, talk tomorrow"). The recovered third-party log /chat/zhangming.log contains three messages by "zhangming" at 21:29, 21:30 and 21:47 (3 deposits totalling 88000 USDT; 5 new platform registrations; "keep maintaining the group tomorrow"). /README.txt explicitly states the device is seized from wangfang, that zhangming is NOT an account on this device, and that zhangming.log was recovered from the same storage volume by the export tool from a previous owner or shared partition. The two logs are interleaved in time (zhangming 21:29-21:30 falls between wangfang 21:05 and 21:31), which is the temporal-trap pattern: proximity only. No message in either log references the other party's content, and there is no shared session, contact handle, transfer, or common identifier. The filesystem timeline is a single cluster of three CREATED events at unix 1790556717 (2026-09-28, i.e. image/export build time, not 2024-04-10), so it cannot order the chat messages against each other. The evidence supports co-location of two logs on one volume; it does not support interaction, causation, or shared intent between wangfang and zhangming.
